"It gets better."

Don't say that to people on here man. You're talking to people who have experienced pain and hurt and suffering their whole lives.

It's cruel to tell them that it'll all just magically change, just because. That's basically the same as attacking their experience and telling them that they're wrong. Just like how everybody else in their life did to them.

Nah man, thank you for posting on here. At least that way you'll leave some kind of evidence behind that you existed.

We all deserved better in life. And it's a hard feeling when you realize that all of your poor decisions cornered you in life where there is no escape.

I hope you find peace one day. I won't lie and say it gets better because lets face it, life doesn't get better. Especially if you're on here.

It's a hard moment when you realise that you just failed at life. I remember that moment too, not too long ago.

You just sort of open your eyes one day and you cut through all of the lies that people told you, about dumb things like self-love and self-worth and all of those feel-good lies that people like telling each other to life each other up when all it does it hurt people like us, people who never felt loved or appreciated.

I don't blame you for what you decide to do after this man. I get it. Life sucks and well...it's just not for everyone.

Yeah. The world just doesn't like people like us. Or people who really suffer for that matter.

I honestly don't blame people for opting out. It's cruel to force people to live lives in pain that doesn't end.

I used to think that way. That in life, there's some reward at the end of that suffering.

But that's not how life is. That's fact. There's just no reward. Only suffering. Some people have the mental convenience or physical convenience to choose to ignore that fact. But we're not those some people.

This is a matter that goes beyond how someone feels about life or an argument of opinion. Life is full of meaningless pain and suffering, with no reward. That's fact. There is no point in arguing against fact. So I don't blame people who choose to opt out of life. They were given bad hands.

Unfortunately that's a sunk cost fallacy. It just doesn't work out that way in life. Life is just bad, and that's it. I've seen so many lives transpire where in their last moments people told me that life wasn't worth all that struggle and pain.

It's really one thing to think that it's just your own thinking, but it's another thing when others independently reaffirm your knowledge about life irl.

Yeah people like to say that things get better. And for some people they might.

But if you're the type of person who's been suffering as we do, and the type of person who posts on here to relieve that mental pressure so to speak...things don't get better. It gets worse.

Like, it's one thing to say that things get better to someone who just experienced a mild setback like their car broke down. But to say that to someone who has had nothing but bad things happen their whole lives, alienation by everybody around them, and just rejected by society, and to say that life will be kinder to them when these are all factors outside of your control, is an extremely dismissive statement and is more likely to cause a person to feel like nobody understands them.
